h: Making a gig night of it in Holmfirth
p: A few tips for getting the best out of a show here. Standing gigs reward an early arrival if you want a good view, while tribute nights tend to fill up fast, so book early if a particular act is coming to town. Earplugs are a smart idea for regular gig-goers, especially in a room with this much atmosphere, and layers are handy because it gets warm once the crowd is in full voice.

Holmfirth's streets are steep and parking in the centre can be tight on busy evenings, so if you're heading in from Huddersfield, which is only a few miles away, a bus or taxi takes the stress out of the night and lets everyone enjoy a drink.

Before the show, have a wander through the town. Sid's Café, made famous by Last of the Summer Wine, is still a magnet for fans, and the little lanes and yards around the centre are full of character. Holmfirth Vineyard, out towards New Mill, is an unexpected Yorkshire treat for anyone fancying a bite to eat with a view.

If you're staying the weekend, the moors above the Holme Valley offer brilliant walking, with reservoirs and big Pennine views. A long walk by day and a loud night at the Picturedrome is a cracking combination.
